§5.5 Embedded Pages

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

layout-embedded-pages · rule layout legal

✅ Normative

A page reproduced inside another page MUST be rendered as the wrapper's furniture followed by the embedded page in its own reading order. Both page numbers MUST be kept, each with its own region, and titles inside an embedded form screenshot MUST NOT be promoted into the wrapper's outline.

A page reproduced inside another page: a statute page shrunk into the middle of an exhibit sheet, a slide placed on a letter-size page. Each carries its own header and page number, so the sheet has two of everything.

      Case 1:23-cv-06750   Document 1-4   Filed 08/02/23   Page 4 of 4     ← wrapper header
                              EXHIBIT D
                          ┌────────────────────┐
                          │   H. R. 2617—507   │  ← embedded header
                          │   (1) The term …   │
                          └────────────────────┘
                              Page 3 of 3                                  ← wrapper footer

Requirements

  • The wrapper's label and filing stamp MUST be kept: they identify the particular copy.
  • The embedded content MUST appear between the wrapper header and the wrapper footer, in the embedded page's own reading order.
  • The wrapper's page number and the embedded page's number MUST both be kept, each where its own band prints it.
  • A title printed inside an embedded form screenshot MUST NOT become a heading of the wrapping document.

Explicit embedded-page boundaries

A producer MAY enclose a reproduced page in <sub_page>…</sub_page>. This is a protocol-defined structural wrapper, not printed text and not a new physical page. Output without the wrapper continues to conform when the required content and reading order are preserved.

  • Each opening <sub_page> MUST have a matching closing tag. Tags MUST be properly nested and MUST NOT cross a physical page boundary. Multiple embedded pages use separate wrappers in reading order; a further nested wrapper is appropriate only when the reproduced page visibly contains another page.
  • The outer page's header, labels and footer MUST remain outside the wrapper. The embedded page's own header, body and footer MUST remain inside it, in their printed reading order.
  • Optional <header> and <footer> bands belong to the nearest enclosing <sub_page>; outside any such wrapper they belong to the physical page. A filename printed below an embedded scan belongs to the outer page, not to the scan's footer.
  • Repeated printed pagination MUST be retained at each printed occurrence. A consumer MUST NOT deduplicate equal page numbers across the outer and embedded pages or across repeated stamps.
  • A consumer that does not use embedded-page structure MUST ignore only the opening and closing wrapper tags, retaining all enclosed content and block boundaries. The wrapper MUST NOT be transcribed as words or interpreted as an instruction to omit its contents.
  • The wrapper does not add a sidecar page, change physical page numbering, or create a new layout element class. Existing elements keep their boxes in the containing physical page's coordinate system. See The Sidecar§3.4 and Block Classes§5.3.

✅ Sample — a court scan inside a faxed page (constructed excerpt)

This boundary-only excerpt follows ParseBench-2's text_ocr__contrast page. The outer fax line prints PAGE 04/29. The embedded court scan prints Page 3 of 28 three times: at its upper right, below its court heading, and at its lower right. The outer page ends with the printed filename court document 2.tiff. The personal case narrative and identifying fields are omitted from this teaching excerpt; omission comments below are editorial and are not printed source content.

Fax line … PAGE 04/29                         ← outer header
┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                         Page 3 of 28     │  ← embedded header
│ IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF BECKHAM          │
│ STATE OF OKLAHOMA                        │
│ Page 3 of 28                             │  ← another printed stamp
│ … case content …                        │
│                         Page 3 of 28     │  ← embedded footer
└──────────────────────────────────────────┘
court document 2.tiff                        ← outer footer

The stamp below the court heading stays at that printed position; it is not moved to the outer page's header. No additional standalone 3 is supplied. The filename is visible text, not merely an image destination: an image link to court_document_2.tiff does not transcribe it.

❌ Counter-sample — treating the embedded page as ignorable content (constructed excerpt)

For the same page, this excerpt loses the court scan and is invalid:

<header>PAGE 04/29</header>
<sub_page></sub_page>
<footer>court document 2.tiff</footer>
Expected Markdown · boundary-only excerpt PAGE 04/29 Page 3 of 28

IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF BECKHAM STATE OF OKLAHOMA Page 3 of 28

Page 3 of 28 court document 2.tiff

<!-- Remaining fax fields omitted from this excerpt. -->
PAGE 04/29
</header>


<sub_page>


<header>Page 3 of 28</header>


IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF BECKHAM
STATE OF OKLAHOMA

<footer>Page 3 of 28</footer>

The correct boundary-only excerpt retains the inner document. A complete transcription must also retain the case content omitted for this teaching example. The presence of <sub_page> never authorizes dropping that content. Ordinary columns, tables and text boxes are not embedded pages merely because a border surrounds them.

✅ Sample — a statute page as an exhibit

A blue e-filing header in four parts, a red EXHIBIT D label, then a reduced statute page with its own running head H. R. 2617—507, and a red Page 3 of 3 at the foot. Expected boxes: four Page-header elements for the e-filing line, Text for EXHIBIT D, a Page-header for the embedded running head, one Text per statute paragraph, and a Page-footer for Page 3 of 3. The colours are decoration and are not carried.
